Data: CelesTrak SATCAT, downloaded September 23, 2026. One row is one cataloged object. Launch year is the year in the launch date column, except that the 416 payloads released from the International Space Station, which carry the station's 1998 launch date, are placed in the year they entered the catalog. In Earth orbit means no decay date and an orbit centered on Earth (objects docked to the space station included), the same definition as the report. Active payloads are payloads with operational status +, P, B, S or X (two rocket bodies that carry the code + are not counted). Perigee and inclination come from the latest cataloged orbit and are left out of medians where the catalog has none; a median drawn in a chart needs at least 15 values. Years since launch run from the launch date (for the payloads released from the space station, the date they entered the catalog) to the decay date, or to September 23, 2026 for objects still up; the report's median years in orbit count only objects that have reentered. Debris labels on the yearly chart name the launch the pieces trace back to, with the same names and counts as the report. The globe draws the objects in Earth orbit that have a cataloged perigee, apogee and inclination (34,496 in the whole catalog); orbital planes and positions along each orbit are assigned at random, since the catalog does not record them.
